html:
The Owen Falls Dam, now the Nalubaale power station, was built across the Nile at Jinja in Uganda, where the river leaves Lake Victoria, and opened by Queen Elizabeth II in April 1954.

It drowned the Ripon Falls that Speke had seen and turned Lake Victoria into a reservoir. Its power supplied Ugandan towns and industry, including a copper smelter, and was sold to Kenya.

A second power station was added in 2000, and the Bujagali dam downstream in 2012. Agreements with Egypt govern how much water may pass, a reminder that the Nile is shared. It was the first great dam of Uganda.
sum: The Owen Falls Dam, now the Nalubaale power station, was built across the Nile at Jinja in Uganda, where the river leaves Lake Victoria, and opened by Queen Elizabeth II in April 1954.
